claims.text: The ductile-brittle-ductile transition in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is driven by non-monotonic L12 long-range ordering in the FCC matrix coupled to changes in B2/FCC interface morphology.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a disordered FCC matrix and B2 intermetallic precipitates and is highly ductile.
Aging near 600°C maximizes the L12 order parameter in the FCC matrix and brings local chemistry toward a stoichiometric Ni3Al ratio.
Increasing L12 order raises the antiphase-boundary energy.
The elevated antiphase-boundary energy at 600°C suppresses cross-slip and promotes planar slip.
Aging near 600°C produces jagged or serrated B2/FCC interfaces through anisotropic interfacial-energy minimization.
Planar slip bands impinging on jagged B2/FCC interfaces form dislocation pile-ups and stress concentrations that exceed interfacial cohesive strength and cause decohesion.
Aging near 750°C lowers the L12 order parameter and antiphase-boundary energy.
Aging near 750°C smooths B2/FCC interfaces or creates disordered interfacial transition zones.
Lower ordering and modified interfaces at 750°C restore cross-slip and ductility.
Elongation falls below 5% after aging at 600°C and recovers above 20% after aging at 750°C.
The brittle state will show planar slip bands terminating at jagged B2/FCC interfaces.
The ductile state will show wavy slip and dislocations penetrating or bypassing B2/FCC interfaces.
The critical L12 order parameter is approximately S = 0.85, with cross-slip active below this value and planar slip dominant above it.
A B2/FCC interface serration amplitude greater than 50 nm is required for the interface to act as the proposed critical stress concentrator.
Local antiphase-boundary energy can be estimated from a critical cross-slip stress derived from dislocation-loop expansion.
Homogenization at 800°C followed by rapid quenching to 600°C will selectively smooth B2/FCC interfaces sufficiently to isolate interface morphology from ordering.
Conventional temper embrittlement attributes brittleness to impurity segregation, such as P or S, at grain boundaries.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says high L12 order and high APBE should produce planar slip even independently of interface serration, whereas falsification rule (1) treats observation of planar slip with a smooth interface as falsifying. A smooth interface should instead test whether planar slip causes decohesion or brittle failure, not whether planar slip occurs.
